newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea details oil deregulation.
newsitem.headline: South Korea details oil deregulation.

text.p: The South Korean government has set certain standards and conditions for the deregulation of domestic oil prices, which takes effect on January 1, 1997.
The following is a summary of the rules and conditions set out by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy.
-- From January 1, 1997, domestic prices of gasoline, kerosene, diesel and C-type fuel will be deregulated and no longer subject to a government-set monthly price ceiling.
-- In the first six months, oil refiners must report intended price changes of gasoline, kerosene and diesel to the government. After six months, refiners can report price changes after the fact.
-- The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy will intervene if prices become too volatile and endanger the stability of the economy.
-- Price-fixing or setting prices artificially low to grab market share will be punished according to the Fair Trade Act.

-- Imports and exports will no longer be the sole domain of refiners. Traders with storage facilities can import/export crude and oil products without seeking government approval. Minimum storage requirements are 60 days of sales volume.
-- Wholesalers and distributors must register with local governments, but no longer need to undergo a vetting process to seek a licence.
